# tests/fixtures — Q4/Q3 fixture sources + generator

Committed sources only. Built outputs live in `out/` and are gitignored.

## Sources

- `firmware.c` — avr-gcc firmware for the device matrix (`-Os -g`).
  Expects `.text` (`main`, touches `PORTB`), `.data`
  (`initialized_value = 0xA5`), `.bss` (`counter_bss`, global `dup_cnt`,
  main-local `static dup_cnt` emitted as `dup_cnt.NNNN`), `.noinit`
  (`preserved_value`), `.eeprom` (`eeprom_value = 0x5A` via `EEMEM`),
  `.symtab`, and `.note.gnu.avr.deviceinfo` (names the `-mmcu` device).
  On XMEGA (`__AVR_XMEGA__`) the `PORTB` touch uses `DIRSET`/`OUTSET`
  because XMEGA `PORTB` is a `PORT_t` struct, not a `uint8_t` SFR —
  fixture-only portability, no product-code special-casing.
- `lib/libutil.c` — one function `libutil_add()` for the static archive.
- `gen.sh` — POSIX sh generator (`set -eu`), see below.

## Outputs (`out/`, generated by `gen.sh`)

- `firmware.elf` — atmega328p fixture: sections + symtab + device note.
- `stripped.elf` — `avr-objcopy --strip-all firmware.elf`: sections kept,
  `.symtab` removed (proves section path without symbols).
- `no_metadata.elf` — `avr-objcopy -R .note.gnu.avr.deviceinfo
  firmware.elf`: device note removed (proves explicit-`--device` path).
- `<device>/firmware.elf` — per-matrix-device firmware (`atmega2560`,
  `attiny85`); same symbols/sections as the 328p build, with
  device-specific VMAs (see table below). (`atxmega128a1` deferred —
  see XMEGA triage.)
- `libfixture.a` — `avr-ar rcs` archive of `libutil.c` (archive path).
- `invalid.bin` — `printf 'not an ELF file\n'` (negative input).
- `host.so` — host `cc -shared -fPIC` 1-function object (negative input;
  only when a host `cc` exists).

The 328p top-level names/paths are frozen: `cli_tests.sh` and
`test_integration` read them via `FIXTURE_DIR` (default `out/`). Q4 tests
address other devices via `out/<device>/`.

## Per-device reference (from `avr-readelf -S`, same toolchain)

| device | `.data` VMA (RAMSTART) | `.eeprom` VMA | `.text` size | note names |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| atmega328p | `0x00800100` (0x100) | `0x00810000` | 0xce | atmega328p |
| atmega2560 | `0x00800200` (0x200) | `0x00810000` | 0x152 | atmega2560 |
| attiny85 | `0x00800060` (0x60) | `0x00810000` | 0x7e | attiny85 |

All three follow the `0x800000 + RAMSTART` data-origin scheme and carry a
standard `AVR` `NT_VERSION` device note — the normalization evidence the
probe relies on. (Sizes are toolchain-self-consistent: same `avr-gcc`
builds the fixture and feeds the probe; re-verify after toolchain
upgrades.)

## XMEGA triage (R8, 2026-09-27): atxmega128a1 deferred, matrix = 3 devices

The xmega ELF itself is healthy — `avr-readelf -S -s -n` on a manually
built `firmware.c` (`-mmcu=atxmega128a1`) shows the standard `AVR`
`NT_VERSION` note naming `atxmega128a1`, data origin `0x800000 + 0x2000`,
and normal `.text/.data/.bss/.noinit/.eeprom/.symtab` sections with the
same `dup_cnt`/`eeprom_value` symbols. The blocker is probe-side, in
avr-libc's xmega headers:

| macro | classic (atmega328p) | xmega (atxmega128a1) |
|---|---|---|
| `RAMSTART` | `(0x100)` | `INTERNAL_SRAM_START` → `(0x2000)` |
| `RAMEND` | `0x8FF` | `INTERNAL_SRAM_END` → `(START+SIZE-1)` |
| `FLASHEND` | `0x7FFF` | `PROGMEM_END` → `(START+SIZE-1)` |
| `E2END` | `0x3FF` | `EEPROM_END` → `(START+SIZE-1)` |

(From `avr-gcc -mmcu=<dev> -E -dM -include avr/io.h`.) The probe's
`get_macro_u32()` parses one numeric literal only
(`src/avr_device_probe.c`), so physical-memory extraction fails and
`bin/avrmem [--device atxmega128a1] --memory <elf>` reports
`probe: physical-memory extraction FAILED` /
`unable to initialize AVR device 'atxmega128a1'` (exit 1). Teaching the
probe chained-macro/expression resolution is product work — no family
hacks in Q3. `firmware.c` keeps its `__AVR_XMEGA__` `PORTB` branch
(manually build-verified); re-adding xmega to `MATRIX_DEVICES` is one
line once the probe supports it.

## Regeneration

From the repo root:

```sh
sh tests/fixtures/gen.sh
```

Idempotent (overwrite ok). Prints `GEN <path>` per emitted file.

## SKIP policy

A missing or incomplete AVR toolchain must never fail the suite:

- Missing `avr-gcc`, `avr-objcopy`, or `avr-ar` → print
  `SKIP: <tool> missing, fixtures not generated`, exit 0.
- 328p `firmware.c` compile failure (e.g. `<avr/io.h>` absent) → print
  SKIP, exit 0 (no further outputs attempted).
- Per-device: unsupported `-mmcu=<dev>` → print
  `SKIP: -mmcu=<dev> unsupported, <dev> fixtures not generated`, emit the
  rest, exit 0.
- Missing host `cc` → skip only `host.so`, rest still generated.

## Never commit `out/`

`tests/fixtures/out/` is gitignored. Commit sources + `gen.sh` only.
